name: sre

findings.message: plugin.sh sources core/claim/claim.sh via a $(cd …) subshell at module-load time, the exact pattern the design explicitly prohibited.
findings.trigger: plugin.sh sourced when ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} contains no directory component (bare filename, e.g. `source plugin.sh` from tests or future callers); `cd ""` fails, `|| true` swallows it, `pwd` returns the caller's working directory; the subsequent `source "$_ccgl_plugin_dir/../../../core/claim/claim.sh"` resolves to a wrong path and fails with 'No such file', aborting every load of plugin.sh on that path. Even in the happy path the `$(cd …)` fork runs on every first load, which the design forbade: "plugin.sh must not source core/claim/claim.sh — that would create a circular dependency and add a startup $(cd ...) subshell in plugin.sh's load path."

findings.message: zbuild_claim_acquire silently swallows both a backend read failure and a label-add failure with no log entry and no event, so a run that proceeds without cross-machine protection leaves no trace of that bypass.
findings.trigger: gh is unauthenticated, rate-limited, or the network is unreachable when a run starts; _zbuild_claim_read_labels_into returns 1; zbuild_claim_acquire returns 0; the run proceeds as if everything is fine; two machines execute the same issue concurrently with no log explaining why cross-machine protection was inactive. The same silence applies on the add path: `_zbuild_claim_add_label_direct "$issue" "zbuild:claimed" || return 0` — a failed add also returns 0 and sets no log. The function's own comment promises "Logs the skip to the run's state dir" but the code does not.

findings.message: zbuild_claim_release swallows every gh failure silently with no event, so when the GitHub API is unreachable at cleanup time zbuild:claimed stays on the issue indefinitely with no explanation visible to operators.
findings.trigger: gh is unreachable or returns non-zero (network failure, rate limit, transient API error) when _runner_abort_trap runs; _ccgl_remove_label exits non-zero; `|| true` discards the error; zbuild:claimed remains on the issue; every subsequent run on that issue is blocked and refused until a human removes the label by hand — but nothing in any log or event tells the operator that release failed or why.

findings.message: zbuild_claim_release never clears _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED, so a second call from the same process passes the guard and silently retries the label removal instead of being a no-op as the design required.
findings.quote:
# Only release if this process acquired the claim
    [[ -z "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED:-}" ]] && return 0

    # Remove zbuild:claimed (advisory; failures never abort the run)
    _ccgl_remove_label "$issue" "zbuild:claimed" || true

    return 0
findings.trigger: zbuild_claim_release is called twice from the same process (e.g. a future change adds a release on a second exit path alongside _runner_abort_trap); on the second call _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED is still set so the guard passes; _ccgl_remove_label calls `gh issue edit --remove-label zbuild:claimed` on a label no longer present; gh returns non-zero; `|| true` swallows it; the design's idempotency invariant — "Unsetting first makes a second call a no-op" — is not met.

findings.message: The DSCLA-9 fixture for the holder's run-status comment is hand-written instead of produced by rsc_render_header, so the test cannot detect a divergence between the writer's format and the reader's regex.
findings.quote:
cat > "$ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE/$_DSCLA9_ISSUE/run-status-comment.txt" <<EOF
<!-- zbuild-run-status run_id=holder-run-prev -->
<!-- zbuild-holder: $_DSCLA9_HOLDER -->
run is in progress
EOF
findings.trigger: rsc_render_header changes the <!-- zbuild-holder: --> comment format (e.g. attribute name or surrounding whitespace); the hand-written fixture keeps the old format; _ccgl_read_holder's regex still matches the fixture; the test passes; in production _ccgl_read_holder no longer matches what rsc_render_header writes; runner output stops naming the holder and DSCLA-9 silently regresses. CLAUDE.md requires: "A test makes such data with the writer's own code… never by hand." The writer here is rsc_render_header in scripts/lib/run-status-render.sh.

reason: the sre lens found a medium or high or critical problem the change introduced
